notes: In «لا يغاير الوجوب المطلق بالذات», the retained electronic A text reads “unrestricted necessity”; the English’s “unrestricted existence” follows the surrounding argument as though «الوجود». This is an explicitly interpretative reading, not an independently established correction.

In the question «نفس معروضه السابق عليه ومقوما له», «مقوما» is coordinated with the predicate of «يكون». The question concerns the apparent paradox that what attaches later could itself constitute its prior subject; the previous English reversed that direction.

groups.note: Further objection announced.
Graded accidental predication apparently gives necessary reality two existences.
Shared meaning premise explained.
Intrinsic instance and attached common existence distinguished in objection.
Necessary’s causal priority includes common existentness.
Reply denies extramental difference of common existentness and reality.
External identity, conceptual addition distinguished.
Objection: divine reality would then attach externally to quiddities.
Reply denies external attachment.
Different shares qualify respective realities.
الماشي is the derivative predicate walker, not walking as a freestanding act.
No separate external universal, despite independent mental consideration.
Attachment restricted to intellect; diverse shares alone external.

corrections.old: Consider walking in relation to its shares in humans, horses, and other things.
corrections.new: Consider the predicate ‘walker’ in relation to its instances in humans, horses, and other things.
corrections.reason: Keep الماشي as a derivative predicate applied to subjects, rather than converting it into the act of walking.

groups.note: Now refutes strengthened Peripatetic counterexample.
Nature either has or lacks real/hypothetical individuals; examples retained.
One or multiple actually existing individuals; second rejected.
Individual intrinsic possibility argument retained; digital وجود بها apparently stands for وجوبها, not independently corrected.
Objection distinguishes possibility of qualification from existence.
Identity of necessary nature and existence collapses that distinction.
Intrinsic possibility persists through externally caused necessity/impossibility.
General possibility allows intrinsic necessity.
English [not established] supplies negative absent from printed فمعلوم; context strongly suggests it but source remains unresolved.
Only non-impossibility yields broad, not strict, possibility.
Reply invokes simple nature, one existing and other impossible individuals.
Modal diversity ruled out by simplicity.
All necessary/all impossible alternatives contradict assumptions.
Necessity entails intrinsic unity; injunction retained.

notes: The electronic A wording has «فمعلوم» where the objection’s following clauses suggest “it is not established”. The existing English’s bracketed negative remains a contextual reconstruction, not an attested variant. The earlier «امتناع وجود بها» is also read contextually as concerning intrinsic necessity.

groups.note: Second branch excludes both mental/intelligible individuals.
Habitual assumption of individuation by extrinsic accidents stated, not adopted.
Several arguments expose habitual beliefs.
First: intrinsic identity of determination makes second individual reversal of reality.
Second: intrinsic entailment of determination excludes other supposed necessary instances.
Conflicting intrinsic necessity/nonexistence yields impossibility.
General-possibility objection preserved in author’s own unusual modal division; no modernization.
Reply distinguishes conceptual conjunction from intrinsic truth of nonexistence.
First two exclude external/intelligible plurality, not necessarily mental representation.
Two additional approaches announced.
Self-determined nature cannot become another intellect’s object under stated framework.
Intellection as unifying relation, not imprinting, retained.
Determination entails distinction and conflicts with such unity.
Second ground: object determined through intellect cannot have second intrinsic determination.
No corresponding intelligible form, hence no plurality of its instances.
Self-determined nature admits no extrinsic conjoined qualifiers.
Both classes of many individuals excluded.
Fourfold classification derived from correspondence requirements.
Absent intelligible or multiple forms; latter absent cause or present hindrance.
Intrinsic/necessarily attached hindrance gives remaining alternatives.
Other-instance predication would transform nature.
Objection: possible supposition of predication suffices for universality.
Reply denies even possible supposition here.
Further objection permits supposing impossible object.
Supposition of impossibility versus impossible supposition preserved exactly.
Previous nonplural necessary nature premise retained.
Essential difference without common meaning would yield equivocity.
Objection: common attribute compatible with essential difference.
Quotation cue, ellipsis and numerous-impossibilities reply retained.
Concrete being neither identity nor part without violating difference/simplicity.
Distinct subject either real quiddity or conceptual matter.
External possible existence could cease or separate from necessary nature.
Self-priority, agent/recipient union and alleged impossibility retained.
Double-existence consequence preserved.
Conceptual cause absent externally while effect exists adds difficulty.
No essential difference gives two entailment alternatives.
Difference of possible existences prevents entailment/share/predication, each requiring unity.
No difference would imply intrinsic entailment of necessary reality.
Intrinsic entailment of Necessary by possibles rejected under opponents’ premises.
Arabic واحدا من جميع الجهات means one in every respect; former English erroneously substituted necessary in every respect.
Accidental difference counterobjection preserved.
Accidents do not differentiate realities, so previous consequences remain.

corrections.old: since otherwise the intrinsically Necessary would not be necessary in every respect.
corrections.new: since otherwise the intrinsically Necessary would not be one in every respect.
corrections.reason: Translate واحدا, not واجبا; argument here concerns unity/simplicity, not merely modal necessity.

notes: At the end of the philosophers’ argument, the retained Arabic reads «ليس واحدا من جميع الجهات». The translation now preserves “one in every respect”; the earlier “necessary in every respect” confused unity with necessity.

groups.note: Opponents’ nonplurality requirement conceded conditionally.
Four exhaustive cases recalled.
None applies to alleged entailing nature; necessary status denied even on existence concession.
Method of granting some opponent premises retained.
Thesis restated.
Required nonplurality and four-case disjunction retained.
First case identified as determination itself.
Determination requires external or mental substrate.
Self-subsistent sustaining nature cannot be dependent attribute.
Positive/negative theories of determination both included.
Objection conditions conclusion on uniform species-nature.
Accidental common predicate could have essentially diverse instances.
Further gradation/equivocity alternatives might allow unknowable independent instance.
Restores conventional invocation abbreviated قده; necessary unity of determination-concept retained.
Relational rather than intrinsic differentiation of instances.
Necessary determination known through its relational aspect.
Knowledge of relation does not require exhaustive essence of terminus.
Aspectual apprehension sufficient and affirmed possible.

corrections.old: We reply that the author has established in his philosophical books
corrections.new: We reply that the author, may his secret be sanctified, has established in his philosophical books
corrections.reason: Represent the conventional invocation abbreviated قده in the retained text.

groups.note: Third nonplurality case challenged.
Unqualified unknowability denied.
Self-knower/intelligible/intellect identity retained.
Cannot deny self-intellection.
Digital لكن مسلّم lacks the negative supplied by English [do not]; surrounding reply suggests conjecture, not established reading.
Known relationally to all intellects, fully to fewer; epistemic degrees distinguished.
Total unknowability would remove form-instance correspondence.
Aspectual/full knowledge cases prevent that consequence.

notes: The electronic A wording «لكن مسلّم» conflicts with the ensuing reply. English “[do not] grant” supplies a contextual negation, explicitly bracketed, not established by independent collation.

groups.note: Fourth nonplurality case challenged.
Other-as-opposite is sheer nonbeing; distinction not from an actual opposite.
Non-opposed relational otherness need not preclude conjunction.
Positive/negative relations conjoined in qualified manner.
Relative multiplicity/world versus considered unity/names retained.
Recall injunction retained.
A fortiori application to opponent’s entailing nature.
Reflection injunction retained.
Two deep objections require intuition and thought free from partisanship/imitation.
First objection’s assumed nonsubsistence of unrestricted nature explicitly attributed.
Conditional established subsistence/necessity would disallow denial or counterinstance.
Demonstrated and self-evident premises separately identified.
Counterinstance’s domain argument preserved without silently rewriting technical naqḍ theory.
Pointless replies prolong discussion and invite challenge; normative pedagogic critique preserved.
Second objection: necessary unrestricted existence could not be shared.
Possible and necessary existences both under common external existence in objection.
Habituated premises loosened by intuition; digital variants in description of cognitive faculties remain unresolved.
Fikr/ḥads analogy with sulūk/jadhba retained, not identity of methods.
Self-subsistent being cannot depend on derivative things; light imagery preserved though reordered.
Evident premise and pedagogical excuse for answering error retained.
Mistaken analogy to other universal natures needing specification.
Opponents infer need for external particularizing/sustaining cause.
Visible light requiring another light analogy retains coloured-surface condition.
Sensory estimation claim rendered with local-example qualification; blind-person comparison preserved.
Intellect dominated by estimation/imagination likened to blindness.
Divine wisdom, guard/watering-place image, Qurʾanic citation, petition and parenthesis marker retained.
Returns to distinction between existence and indeterminate quiddities.
Particular-necessary alternative granted dialectically for rebuttal.
Removing impediments benefits acute readers and becomes instructional duty.
Ordinary syllogistic arrangement contrasted with further intuition/taste.
Selective pedagogical benefit qualified, not universal promise.
Target audience combines discernment, strong intuition and experiential unveiling.
Even without dialectical necessity, clearing doubts prepares receptive students.
Takhliya identified as removing entrenched cognitive impediments.
Taḥliya as positive preparation through certain premises distinguished.
Contrasts jalāʾ and istijlāʾ by predominance of essential unrestrictedness versus name-relative determinations.
The electronic text repeats part of the preceding contrast in a detached string; English does not duplicate it. Retain as a source-level repetition, not a certified omission.
Hiddenness and manifestation are relationally inverted; creator/creation language belongs to an actor-object distinction.

Creation couples holy receptivities fixed in the first determination with manifest existence/Breath. Preserve the source’s own first-determination wording rather than imposing a different doctrinal scheme.
Child/parents and conclusion/premises analogies explain conjoined production; pronoun referent is affected by the reported إليهم/إليهما alternative.
World/creation naming and the preliminary nature of this discussion are retained.
Unmediated act, intelligible relations, exalted letters and keys of the unseen concern the first determination.
Second determination involves relations; the sayings of sages are distinguished from the realizer’s terminology.
Inscription belongs to knowledge as relationally differentiated, not to the unqualified essence.
Intelligible letters/words/fixed entities and divine realities/names are distinguished; displayed existential-letters wording is not silently changed.
Mediated act requires instrument or locus; saying, bringing into existence, the Quranic citation and possible entities are retained.
World of command and the First Intellect retain the quiddity/existence composition even at the simplest created level.
Spirits are the first independent worlds in contrast to meanings existing by consideration.
The world of meanings is a world in a restricted conceptual sense, not another independently subsisting domain.
Imaginal composition and bodily spatial composition add successive restrictions.
The maximum of multiplicity and manifestation is related to reversal of the initial order.
Throne and istiwāʾ are explained through the author’s maturity analogy; this is his interpretive argument, not an independently established lexical gloss.
Four comprehensive levels plus the human fifth are enumerated.
Five determined presences are distinguished from six when the hidden nondetermined level is counted.
The Breath pervades the levels.
Five human articulatory origins correspond to the worlds; teeth/lips alternatives remain source-reported.
Letters, words, verses, suras and books form distinct levels of aggregation.
Torah, Gospel, Psalms and Furqan are distinguished and the Quran assigned comprehensiveness in the author’s scheme.
Universal, generic and specific distinctions explain the classification rather than modern biological taxonomy.
Four natural qualities and temperament are separately included.
Heat, moisture, cold and dryness correspond to the names in a historical cosmological framework.
Acknowledges mysteries and directs reflection rather than offering a full proof.
Subdivisions of spirits, imagination and bodies are distinguished.
The final referral to natural/philosophical disciplines is retained and the omitted authorial invocation رحمه الله restored.

corrections.old: The author therefore refers their discussion to those disciplines.
corrections.new: The author, may God have mercy on him, therefore refers their discussion to those disciplines.
corrections.reason: Restore رحمه الله at the explicit authorial attribution.

notes: Electronic-source comparison (11 Nov 2026): the detached repeated clause following the jalāʾ/istijlāʾ contrast is preserved in Arabic but not repeated in the English reading text. Its status requires source-image or independent-witness inspection.

groups.note: The commentator announces removal of doubts against the preceding account.
Six objections are announced.
First objection: possibility requires a subject capable of being qualified.
Necessary existence cannot itself be a possible subject.
Quiddities regarded as nonbeing cannot supply an independently actual subject.
Even conceptually posited possibility is argued to require a receptive subject.
Second objection: necessitation and requirement seem to require two actual relata.
Third objection divides manifestation between existence, entities and qualified forms.
Absolute existence cannot be said to require itself as another product.
External qualified being, nonbeing and their aggregate are examined under the question of making.
Intellectual existence, identity of instances, qualifications and their aggregate receive the parallel objection.
Entities are said by the objector to be unable to receive being.
Fourth objection asks how worlds differ and considers three proposed grounds.
Fixed entities alone are denied the power to ground actual differentiation.
Undifferentiated existence alone is denied as source of multiple distinct worlds.
The aggregate or configuration likewise fails on the objector’s assumptions.
Undifferentiation/differentiation is challenged where subject and conditions are allegedly unchanged.
Fifth objection reports the Peripatetic denial of the imaginal world; not the commentator’s final position.
The objection invokes credibility of established cognitions against imaginal claims.
Sixth objection challenges greater manifestation at lower levels.
Proximity to the cause is claimed by the opponent to afford greater effects.
Incorruptible intellects and souls are contrasted with sensible and imaginal limitations as part of the objection.

notes: Voice-boundary review (11 Nov 2026): the six numbered difficulties, including the polemic against the imaginal world, are objections being assembled for subsequent reply; they are not six final conclusions of Ibn Turka.

groups.note: Rebuilds the account’s foundations before replying.
The subject of possibility is located in relative determinations.
The Arabic sentence beginning الإمكان عبارة عن الوجود is disordered; English explains the received wording and its difficulty rather than purporting to restore continuous authorial syntax.
States and attributes delimit the known object.
Conjunction with existence gives necessity under that relation.
Considered in themselves, determinations claim neither existence nor nonexistence.
Lack of entitlement to existence is distinguished from entitlement to nonexistence.
English follows a reported interpretive alternative concerning intrinsically required nonbeing, not a demonstrated manuscript correction of عدم الاستحقاقية مطلقا.
Draws the conclusion concerning possibility and relative qualification.
States require existence at the appropriate level, not independent necessary entities.
External, intellectual and unrestricted subjects are carefully distinguished.
Existence is not made identical with or a constituent part of the determinations as determinations.
Turns explicitly to the questioner’s premises.
Quiddities considered in themselves differ from their extrinsic existence; causal relation is explained through dependence.
The monistic objection is reported before its answer.
Knowledge concerns the One’s states, not the One precisely as unqualified.
Incidental attribution, conceptual relations and stripping attributions in tawhid are distinguished.
Preserves authorial pointers and injunction not to overlook the distinction.
Attributed existentness may be conceptual and admit negative properties.
Critics are said to confuse real existence with cognitive properties; the instruction to understand is retained.
Concluding blindness/cross-eyed polemic is the author’s analogy, not a modern diagnostic claim.
Announces replies to the second and third objections.
Manifestation is not defined as ex nihilo manufacture or merely uncovering a sensible object.
Absolute unity, lacking relations precisely as such, has no manifestation in that respect.
Even hiddenness is relational; the hidden-treasure saying is reported as the author’s citation, not authenticated here.
Hiddenness itself presupposes a conceptual descent from the unqualified.
Manifestation is explained as descent into qualifications.
An opposing receptive term permits manifestation in an effect-form.
Sunlight and opaque/transparent bodies illustrate the historical physical model rather than a new empirical argument.
Natural qualities, agency, reception and mixture make the analogy explicit.
Possible determinations nonexistent through themselves can be recipients of existence.
Objection denies intrinsic being and nonbeing alike.
Reply distinguishes absence of a cause from an intrinsic positive cause of nonbeing.
Externally caused nonbeing is not intrinsic impossibility.
Second objection answered through relational causality in determinations.
Third objection answered by attributing manifestation to determinations.
Counterobjection is retained as a distinct voice.
Determinations considered alone differ from their conjunction with existence.
Multiplicity and nonentity belong to the determinations, unity and being to their subject; manifestation concerns their conjunction.
Identifies the fifth objection.
Reuses the fourth reply’s method and example.
Imaginal/witnessed relation modeled on unrestricted/restricted establishes existence, not full nature.
The work expressly declines an account of the imaginal world’s essence.
The treatise’s principal tawhid objective is already established in its argument.
The comparative question gives rise to subsidiary doubts.
The example answers the simple question whether such a world exists.
Detailed essences of either domain are not prerequisites of this limited comparison.
Announces the fourth reply.
Sensory habituation is said to restrict comprehension of higher levels.
Suggestive premises and examples are distinguished from an exhaustive demonstrative account.
The demonstration is expressly limited to possibility or non-impossibility.
Introduces the illustration.
Taste can be sufficient for a qualified recipient while additional premises may not persuade another.
Unrestricted nature’s external/intellectual manifestation is interpreted through the love relation.
External individuation requires determinate subsistence and dimensions.
Place, figure and colour are secondary limits.
Independent substantial natures are distinguished from dependent forms.
Received Arabic repeats the incomplete-nature formulation in adjacent forms; English renders the sense once. No authorial deletion is established.
Quantity and quality are the given examples of dependent realities.
Intellectual existence is placed on the dependent side of this analogy.
The hierarchy distinguishes substance from accident.
The illustration is applied analogically to levels of existence.
The reader is asked to reflect on the distinction.
Meanings are free from particular formal/external limitations.
Unrestricted being differs from externally, intellectually and imaginally determined forms.
Meanings are distinguished from witnessed and imaginal entities.
Unrestricted-to-restricted relation is the controlling analogy.
Unrestricted here embraces external and intellectual being; it is not the wholly unqualified absolute to which nothing accrues.
The discussion proves only existence in outline, not essence. Preserve the displayed referenced title al-Ḥikma al-Manīʿa rather than making it generic elevated wisdom.

corrections.old: The author therefore refers the detailed investigation to the philosophical work designated here as the elevated wisdom [the wording is textually uncertain].
corrections.new: The author therefore refers the detailed investigation to al-Ḥikma al-Manīʿa [the displayed title, whose textual form remains uncertain].
corrections.reason: Preserve الحكمة المنيعة as a displayed work-title, without claiming independent bibliographic or manuscript identification.

notes: Electronic-source comparison (11 Nov 2026): the repeated incomplete-nature phrase is retained in Arabic and represented once in the English. The final displayed work-title is الحكمة المنيعة; its identification and textual form have not been independently established.

groups.note: Sixth and final objection is addressed.
Greater perfection concerns the diversity of manifestations and effects.
An effect is a form and locus of its cause.
More modes of reception yield more complete manifestation in the chosen illustration.
Existence and life are the broad initial cognition.
Sensation, motion and rational speech specify essential apprehension.
Universality is distinguished from subsequent restricted modes.
The remote image presents quantitative, qualitative and positional determinations.
Estimative relations such as parenthood and love are retained.
Present sensory apprehension is a further mode.
The combination gives comprehensiveness.
One determination gathering these modes is identified as the goal.
Gathering of gathering is preserved as the technical name.
Humanity combines active cognition with material receptivity; mere embodiment does not supply the whole account.
Appearing and making appear are jointly required.
Human cognition is said to gather all the stated modes.
Other intellects and souls lack this specific diversity in the author’s argument.
Two forms of comprehensiveness are distinguished.
The two seas are receptivity and agency.
The two bows are necessity and possibility.
Further explanation and God-willing qualification are retained.
Objection: the general question is not settled by a human-only example.
Reply generalizes the example rather than denying the objection’s scope.
Animals, plants, minerals and elements illustrate the wider order of manifestation.
Comprehensive manifestation and an effect-based innī proof are distinguished.
The limmī explanation relates hidden unrestricted reality and manifested names.
Contingent qualifications and mutual reflection account for cumulative differentiation.
A lower level adds its own restrictions while containing prior levels’ restrictions.
Greater breadth of manifestation is the stated sense of greater completeness.
Human comprehensiveness and vicegerency retain the conditional future elaboration.
The school’s agreed position is identified as such.
School postulates cannot simply be imposed on opponents; the proposed effect-based explanation is qualified as perhaps intended.
First objection: if diverse apprehension perfects, why do guides restrain sensory activity? Preparatory cause versus impediment is retained.
Second objection: death would deprive a soul of its perfecting bodily instruments.
Reply distinguishes apprehension as such from training stable capacities so sensory restrictions do not obstruct higher modes.
A more comprehensive inward apprehension is compared to a genus containing its species, not equated with ordinary psychic cognition.
Unrestricted reality, hidden disclosure, preparedness, eternal knownness, will and the quoted creative command remain distinct steps.
Existential orientation is determined by receptivity and explains accompaniment, sustaining presence and replenishment.
Longing and affinity between possible and necessary depend on that relation.
Inward spiritual cognition receives aid from essential knowledge through the name Hidden.
Source says from the level of Manifest and immediately not from that level. English flags the contradiction rather than silently resolving the negation.
Wayfaring absorbs multiplicity into comprehensive unities and the fixed entity; witnessing/knowledge and disclosed union are distinguished.
Spiritual and bodily faculties acquire the disclosure’s character; a new comprehensiveness of cognition is contrasted with familiar psychic and bodily modes.
Acquired unveiling/holy faculty, deliberate effort, refinement and invitation to reflection all retained.
Quoted ancestral response about death and perfected souls is preserved; isolated punctuation fragments belong to an ellipsis, not missing semantic clauses.
Acquired perfectional dispositions survive the instruments that prepared them; instruments may subsequently impede operation.
Full explanation of the intermediate world is explicitly deferred.
Moves from tawhid and its foundations to the treatise’s goal of human comprehensiveness.
Absolute unity comprehends relative unity/multiplicity and opposites, rather than being one numerical member.
No contrary or peer and one without number are distinguished from unity opposed to plurality.
Relative unity differs negatively from absolute unity while plurality adds restrictions; relative unity’s priority is preserved.
Predominance of unity/multiplicity governs manifest/hidden existential effects.
Inclusive determination of whole/general differs from mutually excluding determination of opposites.
Spirits/images and opposed elemental natures illustrate differing predominance, within the author’s historical cosmology.
Breaking elemental opposition leads through mineral, vegetal and animal receptivities toward human manifestation.
Explicit appeal to reflection retained.
Essential unity subdues name-multiplicity in the comprehensive determination.
Breath, articulation and particulars explain dispersed manifestations and name-perfection.
Restore explicit intellectual differentiation and its grounding in the essence, alongside external articulation.
Complete human locus embraces luminous names, shadowy cosmic realities, inward and outward relations.
Neither unqualified unity nor dispersed cosmic parts separately exhibits both sides of comprehensiveness.
Balanced elemental human constitution joins divine unrestrictedness and servantly restriction.
Restores the invocation قدس سره in attribution to the Shaykh before the separately identified quotation.
Quoted outward and inward copies correspond respectively to cosmos and divine presence.
Within the quotation the cosmos is servant, God alone divine, and originated attributes do not qualify Him.
Humanity’s two relations, obligation/vicegerency and isthmus/mirror boundary are preserved.
Source gives two overlapping formulations of unrestricted perfection in origination and eternity. English renders the complete sense once; possible duplication remains uncollated.
Eternal and originated perfections are distinguished, followed by human comprehensiveness and praise.
Opposed human exemplars remain within the quoted authority; restore blessings on Muhammad and peace upon Moses.
Highest/lowest human stations and the final divine incomparability citation close the quotation.
Author explicitly closes the quotation, then calls for inward refinement and seeks divine enabling.

corrections.old: Unity is consequently concealed through differentiation and external articulation, which display the particular perfections belonging to their particulars.
corrections.new: Unity is consequently concealed, as the essence requires intellectual differentiation and external articulation, to display the particular perfections belonging to their particulars.
corrections.reason: Retain العقلي and بحسب اقتضاء الذات; not undifferentiated generic differentiation.

corrections.old: The Shaykh expressly states this in his treatise The Construction of Circles.
corrections.new: The Shaykh, may his secret be sanctified, expressly states this in his treatise The Construction of Circles.
corrections.reason: Restore قدس سره.

corrections.old: Yet how base and sullied it can also be in existence, for from it have come Muḥammad, Abū Jahl, Pharaoh, and Moses.
corrections.new: Yet how base and sullied it can also be in existence, for from it have come Muḥammad, may God bless him and his family, as well as Abū Jahl, Pharaoh, and Moses, peace be upon him.
corrections.reason: Restore صلى الله عليه وآله and عليه السلام in the cited passage.

notes: Quotation-boundary review (11 Nov 2026): the passage from Inshāʾ al-Dawāʾir remains a quotation embedded in Ibn Turka’s commentary, not an independent collation of that work. The overlapping phrases about unrestricted perfection remain a source-level duplication question.

groups.note: Only elemental human constitution is proposed as complete locus across disclosure and self-beholding.
Objection: primordial self-knowledge already contains every level, making further manifestation redundant.
Reply distinguishes knowledge identical with essence from additional differentiated knowing; knower, known and knowing are not separate here.
Necessity/possibility and name distinctions arise at another relational level.
Breath, particularizing will, preparedness and intermediaries are separately rendered.
Ordered higher-to-lower receptivity retained; explicitly preserve technical توقيفية rather than replacing it with appointed domains alone.
Vegetal/animal succession is the given matter/form illustration.
Intermediaries here are ordered preparednesses, not independent separated efficient causes; dispersed manifestation still incomplete.
Otherness and name-effects do not yet yield self-apprehension through complete gathering.
Spiritual versus bodily modes and other particulars differ in their specific determinations.

corrections.old: The names have their appointed domains: attaining the higher prepares for attaining the lower.
corrections.new: The names have a tawqīfī, authoritatively fixed character: attaining the higher prepares for attaining the lower.
corrections.reason: Preserve الأسماء توقيفية as an explicit technical claim, with its contextual consequence.

notes: Terminology review (11 Nov 2026): tawqīfī renders توقيفية. In this passage the author connects it with ordered preparedness and higher/lower manifestations; the translation does not independently settle how that use relates to the usual doctrine of divinely authorized naming.

groups.note: Announces philosophical objections to the human terminus of the existential movement.
Objector proposes divine self-sufficiency, or alternatively the sufficiency of the First Intellect.
Presence of essence to itself and of the first effect with its differentiated forms are distinct claims.
Necessitation, presence and bestowed forms ground the objection’s argument.
Already possessing comprehensive and differentiated knowledge is argued to make the proposed goal redundant.
Nested counterproposal invokes detailed cognition of particulars rather than only universals.
The objector’s nested reply grants cognition of particulars universally while denying mutable deficient cognition.
The author’s next lemma is identified as addressing that reply; trailing punctuation marks are ellipsis fragments.

notes: Dialectical-voice review (11 Nov 2026): this unit formulates objections, including a nested reply about universal cognition of particulars. These sentences must not be detached and represented as Ibn Turka’s final adjudication.

groups.note: Neither first gathering nor second differentiation alone provides the comprehensive locus.
Prior specifying knowledge grounds volitional impulsion, contrasted with involuntary Peripatetic necessitation.
Inward human reality and outward elemental constitution are distinguished under the universal-locus account.
Command and existential movement are clear; the contrasting printed النسى is explicitly uncertain in English.
Circular return retained and omitted إن شاء الله تعالى restored.
Replenishment descends through Pen, Tablet, Throne, Footstool, spheres, elements and generated beings to the human.
Conditional ascent and return to the original isthmic level close the circle; no automatic attainment by every individual asserted.
Reflection and inward/outward orientation are explicit.
Perfect Human joins essence-manifestation and names/attributes/acts through balance and receptivity.
Necessary/possible and divine/created relations are gathered without erasing their distinct considerations.
Grammatical dependence of so that He may manifest upon was impelled preserved.
The universal comprehensive affair is the proposed unique locus.
Self-apprehension through complete gathering is the stated end of loving existential pervasion.

corrections.old: Know, then, that the divine relation, in accordance with essential unity, requires the movement bringing things into existence to be circular and returning, as will be explained.
corrections.new: Know, then, that the divine relation, in accordance with essential unity, requires the movement bringing things into existence to be circular and returning, as will be explained, God Most High willing.
corrections.reason: Restore إن شاء الله تعالى.

groups.note: Restore the invocation at the explicit attribution to Muḥyī al-Dīn and keep the Fuṣūṣ reference.
Self-seeing without a distinct locus differs from seeing through a mirror that supplies a form.
The recipient supplies an influence determining the form; English previously reversed this into the recipient receiving that influence.
Restore al-Ḥallāj’s full displayed name and the authorial epithet before the poetic citation.
Objection proposes First Intellect as distinct intellectual mirror.
The alternative of sensible particular cognition is distinguished from intrinsic/incidental visibility.
Bodily-accident clause is repeated in the electronic source; English renders the optical argument once and no textual deletion is certified.
Incidental visible object is body or bodily material.
Commentator challenges confinement of mediated cognition to bodily accidents by invoking universal after plurality.
Abstraction from sensory forms blocks a blanket denial of mediated apprehension.
Nested objection concerns material qualifiers and the Necessary as necessary.
Reply places sensible clothing in the locus-relative conditions of manifestation.
Nonapplication of Necessary does not entail invisibility of the reality; explicitly retain the technical tawqīfī naming claim.
The Shaykh says Real under the beautiful names, not Necessary without qualification.
Reported Imam saying and Shaykh verses support his argument; their attribution is represented without independently authenticating the reports.
Proximity through supererogatory works and unqualified reality are different registers; intellect and sense equally fail in the latter respect.
Restore رضى الله عنه for Ghazālī inside the quoted passage while retaining its explicit rejection of affinity.
Source حتى يتوهم is rendered as lest it be mistaken, supplying a contextually expected negation. Keep this interpretation marked pending independent witness.

corrections.old: I say: this refers to what Shaykh Muḥyī al-Dīn says in the Bezels of Wisdom, intimating an answer to the preceding difficulty.
corrections.new: I say: this refers to what Shaykh Muḥyī al-Dīn, may his secret be sanctified, says in the Bezels of Wisdom, intimating an answer to the preceding difficulty.
corrections.reason: Restore قدس سره.

corrections.old: the form's particular character follows upon the recipient's reception of that influence.

groups.note: Challenges exclusive suitability of First Intellect as mirror.
A complete mirror would need a relation and share corresponding to every level, without distortion.
Comprehensive being, not one-level intellect, is proposed as meeting that condition.
Possible cosmic receptivities and necessary name-receptivities both have counterparts in the Perfect Human.
Counterreply denies that every human actually discloses every level; the universal conclusion is challenged through individual variation.
The objector concludes that some names remain only intellectually known and the proposed complete mirror has not been established.

notes: Voice review (11 Nov 2026): the counterreply beginning وجواب ذلك remains an objection to be answered, not the commentator’s final denial of human comprehensiveness.

groups.note: Continues an objection against mirroring in general, even by the macrocosm.
Three alternatives: human reality, unrestricted existence, existence with all determinations; an exclusive determination was already excluded.
First alternative allegedly destroys difference between mirror and mirrored.
Second gives every existent suitability, including a prior and enduring intellect, not uniquely humanity.
Third proposes the whole cosmos with collective form; sensory/intuitive faculty variant remains explicitly indicated.
Analogy of natural unity to macrocosm is an objection; displayed reference to questioner is retained with caution.
Past, present and future species/events undermine simultaneous exhaustive embodiment in the objector’s argument.
No one individual is claimed to encompass infinitely varying human perfections.
Explains the conditional consequent; isolated dots are punctuation from a quoted ellipsis.
Unique perfections of Seal of Prophets and Seal of Friends serve as the objector’s internal challenge.
Continues, rather than endorses, the objection against mirroring by the macrocosm.
If comprehensive self-apprehension were not intrinsic perfection, it could not function as final cause and object of divine love.
If it is perfection, the objector alleges dependence on an originated possible locus, contradicting necessity in all respects.
Nested response says the other as other is nonexistent and cannot ground necessary perfections.
Nested counterresponse appeals to multiple receptivities and their relations of conjunction, incompatibility and opposition.
Turns from theoretical to practical objections.
The opponent describes release from acquired restrictions as condition of unrestricted apprehension.
On that premise bodily operation must cease lest material limitations contaminate apprehension.
Displayed الكفرية is rendered discursive as though الفكرية in the enumerated faculties. This is contextual interpretation, not witnessed Arabic correction.
A further objection argues moral perfection removes the demon/beast counterparts required by comprehensiveness.
Celestial incorruptibility and continuous motion are historical cosmological premises of the opponent.

notes: Electronic-source review (11 Nov 2026): the list of faculties prints الكفرية where discursive requires الفكرية. The English follows the contextual faculty-list reading; Arabic is not silently emended.

groups.note: Preserve both conclusions: unattainability and consequent alleged impossibility, not merely failure to acquire.
Opponent constrains intellect to its special sphere like other faculties.
Sight/sound analogy and a fortiori exclusion of bodily faculties are retained.
The argument links verbal signification to prior intellectual, mnemonic and imaginative representation.
Contraposition from expressibility to possibility is represented as the opponent’s argument, not accepted without reply.
Another objection confines detachment to death and denies that contrary acts remove natural dispositions.
Mere sustained contemplation is argued not to remove natural concomitants.
The objection finally claims even death leaves some inherent restrictions.

corrections.old: Their absolute perfection would therefore be unattainable.
corrections.new: Their absolute perfection would therefore be unattainable, and thus impossible.
corrections.reason: Restore فيكون ممتنعاً after the distinct unattainability conclusion.

groups.note: Returns to the opening pathological-certainty objection.
Balanced demonstrative cognition is the objector’s standard of genuine perfection.
A conditional polemical reversal targets repeated loud utterance and alleged dissipation of psychic spirits.
Withdrawal, dark places, diet, imagination and dryness belong to the historical humoral objection, not modern medical advice.
Black bile, false perceptions and symptom inference remain explicitly reported allegations.
The objection’s account of self-opposition, forced dispositions and blame-associated conduct is retained.
It characterizes these traits as deficiency rather than the mean and as depriving joy.
Alleged illness, weakness and preparation for death are preserved.
Conclusion that such perceptions are false is still the opponent’s, not final authorial judgment.
Begins ordered replies to the alleged priority of cognitive determination, First Intellect or macrocosm over humanity.
Complete locus requires copies of every level, while each particular appears according to its proper level.
Oneness of gathering-of-gathering is added to possession of all level-copies; neither condition is omitted.
Embedded verse about the essence/core and subtlety of everything in the collection is retained.
First cognitive determination has undifferentiated unseen knowledge without internal distinctness.
First Intellect has distinct forms but only according to its own specific level.
Macrocosm has external differentiation but lacks oneness of gathering-of-gathering.
Human constitution is claimed to combine all levels with maximal comprehensive oneness.
Concludes that complete manifestation as such requires the human locus.
Reprised objection reads تعقلا عينيا تفصيليا rather than the earlier unseen cognition wording; English marks the displayed reprise rather than silently harmonizing it.
First cognition is through essence in a comprehensive affair, including necessary names and possible realities.
Second cognition is through loci, differentiated and appropriate to each level.
Intellectual, estimative and imaginative cognition correspond to universal and particular receptivities.
Sensory cognition concerns formal and external individuating attributes.
Senses intrinsically concern cosmic forms; names and necessary realities only incidentally and mediately, thus one bow of the circle.
The human collection surveys every level by its copy and combines gathered and differentiated knowledge.
Instruction to reflect and final verse are retained separately from explanatory prose.
At first determination multiplicity is enfolded and opposed names including form are not attributed.
Second determination distinguishes knowledge/existence, hidden/manifest and necessity/possibility, permitting form-language.
Selects existence with all determinations from the standpoint of active effects.
Objection says agency would include only some determinations and fail to be form of whole.
Reply includes every determination from the side of action rather than reception.
Same relations differ by attribution to Principle or acts/receptivities, yielding active form and receptive human locus.
Long received sentence repeats the real-combination/intermixture phrase; English represents the combined sense once. No witnessed deletion is established.
First horn of objection: real identity destroys the difference between manifest and locus.
Second horn: privileging active determinations looks arbitrary and compromises comprehensiveness; both horns remain before قلنا.
Reply distinguishes necessary/principial and possible/created considerations in differentiation.
Unrestricted comprehensiveness belongs to gathering, not to collapsed differences within differentiation.
Hidden, manifest, loci and concealments are one by unrestricted reality but distinct relationally; final cross-reference and injunction retained.
Replies to prioritizing the macrocosm rather than an individual locus.
Particular elemental portions can form balanced bodies through interaction of opposed qualities; cosmological physiology remains attributed.
Overcoming opposition permits manifestation of necessary properties through organs, powers and coordinated actions.
Soul/body form-matter relation and temperamental bond ground real natural specific unity.
Simultaneous contrary-direction operations, nutrition, sensation, thought and longing illustrate a unified composite.
Plural principles as plural and the cosmos’s entire elements/spheres cannot produce the same naturally unified composite.
Lack of common temperament permits only aggregative unity, not the required natural unity.
Objection appeals to mineral, vegetal, animal and human temperaments already within the cosmos.
Reply concedes cosmic manifestation through humanity but denies an independently sufficient macrocosm.
The two poles, unifying necessity and possible multiplicity, require a balanced comprehensive locus.
Explicit instruction to reflect retained.
Author expressly classifies most premises here as persuasive and defers fuller demonstration; do not overstate their proof-status.
Restates objection concerning inferior kinds supposedly absent from human comprehensiveness.
Nourishment/growth rendering uses an indicated correction of displayed الكمية; not a newly collated reading.
Intentional noble acts versus incidental deficient acts distinguish the kinds within the author’s teleological classification.
Finite noble kinds end in the intended goal; superior kinds include inferior perfective acts but not conversely.
Real unity can encompass kinds without enumerating their indefinitely many individuals.
Specific comprehensiveness is distinguished from individual variation and the objection from the two seals.
Temporal increase of perfections and completion in the seal are retained; restore the explicit blessing on the seal.
Closer temporal affinity is said to increase reception, not a universal modern theory of progress.
Ancient Persian المتألهة are sages devoted to divine wisdom, not themselves divinized/deified; the illumination analogy is preserved as a reported argument.
Restore the invocation on the Prophet within the time-cycle report, without independently authenticating the quoted report.
The completing individual differs from lesser impeded realizations; extensive premises are deferred.

corrections.old: Each succeeding perfected person must encompass the predecessor's perfections together with the particular perfections proper to himself, until that kind of perfection is completed in the seal.
corrections.new: Each succeeding perfected person must encompass the predecessor’s perfections together with the particular perfections proper to himself, until that kind of perfection is completed in the seal—upon him be the finest blessings and the fullest greetings.
corrections.reason: Restore عليه من الصلوات أفضلها ومن التحيات أكملها.

corrections.new: This is supported by what is reported of the ancient Persian sages devoted to divine wisdom: they agreed that, as the ranks of intellects descend, their illuminations multiply.

groups.note: Objection alleges that manifestation entails dependence incompatible with necessity through self.
Reply distinguishes required determinations arising from the Real Himself from external dependencies.
Counterobjection stresses the possible character of particular determinations.
Relative name-perfection may involve possible determinations, unlike intrinsic necessary perfection and absolute self-sufficiency.
Dependence for manifestation is distinguished from dependence for existence/necessity; all necessary-through-Him qualifiers are retained.
Genuine unrestrictedness gathers all restrictions and is not simply their absence; explicit reminder retained.
Begins practical replies by distinguishing release from restrictions from loss of comprehensiveness.
Intrinsic unrestrictedness includes restriction and its absence; sensory faculties therefore remain relevant.
Holy faculty orders the bodily faculties and their operations.
Displayed لا اعتبر is interpreted as conditional لاعتبر; English keeps positive inclusion, but independent text-check is still required.
Faculties assist and prepare perfection; restore final فاعلم ذلك.
Demon/beast counterparts remain but are refined, not annihilated or independently indulged.
Reported prophetic saying and animal counterparts retained; restore blessing on the Prophet.
Analogy need not match every individuating feature; arteries and lungs illustrate inherited cosmic physiology, not present-day empirical claims.
Restore sanctification formula before separately attributed Shaykh quotation.
Four worlds and their macrocosmic/human domains are enumerated.
Muhammadan Reality/life, subtle reality/holy spirit, Throne/body, Footstool/soul, House/heart and angels/spirits kept in order.
Seven planetary faculty/organ correspondences are faithfully preserved within the quotation.
Four elemental qualities, humours and nutritive faculties are retained as a historical correspondence scheme.
Seven coloured earth layers correspond to seven bodily layers in the stated sequence.
World of inhabitation/life-and-death and spiritual, sensitive, vegetal and mineral counterparts are distinguished; title variant remains unresolved.
Place example uses a reported neck/shoulder alternative rather than displayed eye wording; attribution and textual uncertainty remain explicit.
Position example يميني/نفسي remains uncertain; acting/eating and receiving/satiation are clear.
Animal images preserved; English cowardly follows a suggested reading rather than displayed جبار. Do not certify the suggested reconstruction as a manuscript reading.
Final instruction and divine guidance formula conclude the embedded quotation.

corrections.new: achieving an effect with assistance is easier than achieving it without assistance—understand this.
corrections.reason: Restore فاعلم ذلك without changing sentence segmentation.

corrections.new: The report that the Prophet’s satan submitted through him—may God bless the Prophet and his family—points to this meaning.

groups.note: Rejects the claim that above discursive intellect means absolutely unintelligible.
Higher assistance can make an object available that intellect then apprehends.
Lower sensory assistance provides the parallel case for particulars.
Received sentence about remaining objects is incomplete; the fluent English is a contextual construction, not a demonstrated restoration.
Any faculty apprehending universal meaning/reality falls under intellect, whether by proof or unveiling.
Ordinary discursive intellect is one power/level of intellect, not its exhaustive definition.
Consequently higher knowledge need not be unthinkable, inexpressible or sheer nonbeing.
Memory, estimation and imagination can obey the higher intellect even where discursive reason lacks mastery.
The author invokes exceptional eloquence as evidence of expressive power, not a proof supplied anew by the editor.
Objection concerns entrenched dispositions and apparent inefficacy of conceptual watchfulness.
Defines sustained attention to unrestricted reality through varied determinations and announces its prerequisites.
One disclosure varies through receptive determinations; restore the divine glorification. Displayed العام is understood as العالم contextually.
English concealed follows a reported alternative to displayed محققا; this affects the polarity and is not independently settled.
Heart comprehends divine and cosmic relations and changes with its contents; the electronic joining-two-seas wording is strained.
Freedom from dominating particular beliefs/names permits essential gathering; knowledge first in rank.
Watchfulness together with ethical discipline subordinates rather than indulges animal faculties.
Disordered source sentence about indulging faculties is interpreted contextually; the English explicitly discloses the defect.
Stronger contrary causes redirect operations; treatment-by-contraries maxim is retained as the author’s explanatory framework.

corrections.old: The Real's replenishments and self-disclosures reach the world continuously at every breath.
corrections.new: The Real’s replenishments and self-disclosures—glorified and exalted is He—reach the world continuously at every breath.
corrections.reason: Restore سبحانه وتعالى.

groups.note: Replies to the humoral-pathology objection by announcing the opposite explanation.
Practices are said to restore disturbed balance, not deliberately damage it; full matn explanation need not be repeated.
Circular form, central reality and opposed name-relations supply the preliminary analogy.
Centre has no counterpart and represents true unity; balanced form is explained through this analogy.
Nearer/further positions differ in unity, multiplicity and comprehensiveness.
Human mean, intellectual simplicity and lower multiplicity are three cosmological classes.
Human individuals likewise divide into balance, excess and deficiency; species capacity is not equated with every individual’s realization.
Opposed corrective tendencies restore the mean; details are referred to the matn.
Distinguishes sophisticated rational investigators from polemical opponents before the author’s own reply.
Peripatetic and non-Peripatetic investigators admit possibility but find conditions difficult.
Removing attachments and sustaining attention are separate challenges.
Restore explicit prophetic attribution and blessing in the report about the changing heart.
Potential bodily imbalance is a reported concern, not a prescription.
Prior universal science and discriminating rules are proposed safeguards against prolonged imagination.
Thirty-year reliance anecdote is preserved as reported; restore sanctification of Husayn ibn Mansur.
Shaykh’s distinction between knowledge and merely clear states, and the sanctuary verse, are retained.
Prior knowledge would disclose error before the traveller settles in it.
Claim of rational inquiry’s priority is the investigators’ reported conclusion, followed next by the author’s disagreement.

corrections.new: The language of revelation expresses this in the Prophet’s saying—may God bless him and his family—that the believer’s heart is between two fingers of the All-Merciful: among bodily members none changes position more readily than the fingers.
corrections.reason: Restore صلى الله عليه وآله and explicit prophetic attribution without authenticating the report anew.

corrections.new: It is reported that al-Ḥusayn ibn Manṣūr, may his secret be sanctified, asked a practitioner about his state and station.
corrections.reason: Restore قدس سره.

groups.note: Author’s own reply begins وأما نحن and asserts shared necessary conditions.
Attention even to first principles requires excluding distractions, a fortiori acquired sciences.
Earlier correction following السهو as lapses of attention is preserved; السهر parallel and الانفعالية/الانتقالية remain distinct source questions.
Purification conditions reasoning, not the reverse; the author allows purification to be independently sufficient.
Possibility is qualified by sound innate disposition, not generalized to everyone.
Distracting thoughts affect both paths, and disciplined imagination is not impossible.
Restore omitted الأصول القويمة literally as sound foundations; its special force among recitation and sound practices remains uncertain.
Swords/storms of realization contrasted with scissors of imitation.
Objection contrasts emptying the heart with active discursive thought.
Reply distinguishes prior formation of dispositions from later emptying particular cognitions and denies absolute indispensability of reasoning.
Purification suffices; reasoning may prepare, as the separately attributed correspondence quotation explains.

corrections.old: Some occupy it with firm recitations and forceful utterance;
corrections.new: Some occupy it with firm recitations, forceful utterance, and sound foundations.
corrections.reason: Restore the otherwise omitted الأصول القويمة without speculative technical reconstruction.

notes: Electronic-source review (11 Nov 2026): sound foundations translates the displayed الأصول القويمة in the list of practices. Its precise technical sense in that context remains unresolved. The prior السهو correction and the distinction from the ancestral السهر are preserved.

groups.note: Now reports the purification-practitioners’ objection that sensory mediation causes error while direct effusion does not.
Reply distinguishes sensory preparation in both routes from the Principle’s intrinsic bestowal.
Without bodily preparation soul-body association would lack its proposed end; death objection follows.
Counterobjection about acquired obstacles and reply about anterior perfection preserve their conditional logic.
Two alternatives are stated explicitly.
Conceding helpful dispositions as well as obstacles concedes the preparatory thesis.
Appropriate use prepares perfection; inappropriate use forms obstructive habits.
Principle bestows while syllogistic premises prepare reception, not independent efficient production.
Recipient’s need is not the agent’s dependence: central causal asymmetry preserved.
Emptying renders the contextual sense of displayed تخيلة as if تخلية; no independent correction of Arabic is claimed.

notes: Layer-boundary review (11 Nov 2026): SH-059 is the surviving descendant’s commentary. Its discussion cannot be substituted for the reported missing ancestral wording at QT-059. The displayed تخيلة/expected تخلية remains a minor electronic-source difficulty.

groups.note: Reconciles the two methods with preceding realization principles.
Heart contains realities بالفعل, in actuality, though their effects are veiled; retain the author’s actual/hidden distinction rather than substitute mere potentiality.
One method orders discursive activity after moral mastery, the other stills faculties after purification; both are affirmed.
Harshā verse and ruler/artisans analogy retained.
First political analogy strengthens ruler and helpers to order assigned operations.
Second method subdues the bodily powers’ auxiliaries and weakens the powers; restore explicit أعوانها instead of generic influence.
Purification is necessary in both, secondarily intended through mastery in first and primarily intended in second.
Polemic targets denial of purification in learning, not reasoning itself.
Supplication and guidance/straying formula preserved.
Final statement that matn is clear closes the commentary unit.

corrections.old: The other removes those bodily powers from their governing positions, stills them, and restrains their distracting movements after subduing and weakening their influence through purification.
corrections.new: The other removes those bodily powers from their governing positions, stills them, and restrains their distracting movements after subduing their auxiliaries and weakening them through purification.
